title: Sgt. Weaver at the scheduling boards
description: Sgt. Weaver — an ex-Marine, Larry says — leans on the quarter-hour flight-scheduling racks inside the pegboard-walled operations van, cigarette in hand, whistle cord around his neck. The boards behind him carry stenciled time blocks and a ruled status chart. Weaver, Larry says, "was a cool guy and hung out with me a lot."
researchNotes: Larry's own identification (Memories comment, 2026-08-15; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0014-c18032226.json). The 2026-08-09 vision survey read the name tape as beginning 'WE…' before he named the man; that is machine output and is recorded as consistent with his identification, not as corroboration of it (the rest of the tape is hidden by the whistle cord). Weaver is also the sergeant (an E5) who responded to the bathroom shooting in Larry's fuller 2026-08-15 account (data/recollections/giscus-stories-c18035411.json). His pocket patch is a magnification target whose lettering sits below this scan's resolution and waits on a high-resolution re-scan of the slide; what can be seen of it is kept in research/magnification/README.md and deliberately not described here, since what the patch said is a question for him (2026-09-14: the shape and colour were removed from this record). 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0014-c18415711.json), with 'Location: Ton Son Nhut': inside the van; the day shift 'probably 4 guys' and the night shift one; Larry on nights a lot 'because I was going to the mountain a lot in Nui Ba Den. I felt safer on the mountain that I did at Ton Son Nhut.' This agrees with the twelve-hour night shifts alone of VN-0015 and gives a reason for them — a man rotating to the mountain took the single-man shift at the base.
